cards.text: Esau and Jacob have just buried their father Isaac (Genesis 35:29). Now Genesis turns from Jacob to his twin brother, Esau (Genesis 25:24-26). And right in the first line, we learn Esau is also called Edom.

First up, Esau's wives, taken from the daughters of Canaan: Adah, Oholibamah and Basemath, daughter of Ishmael, Abraham's son. They give Esau five sons, all born in the land of Canaan. Grab a pencil, friend, because this family tree is about to get BUSY.

Later, Esau rounds up his wives, his sons and daughters, and every person in his household to MOVE. Friend, folks beg three buddies and a borrowed truck just to move one apartment, and this man is moving a WHOLE household.

cards.question: True or false: Esau leaves his livestock behind in Canaan.
True or false: Esau moves to a land far away from his brother Jacob.
Why can't Esau and Jacob keep living in the same place?

answers.text: They own too much for the land to support
They have another fight over a blessing
God tells Esau to leave the land of Canaan

cards.text: So Esau, also called Edom, settles in the area of Mount Seir.

Then Genesis starts Esau's account again, and out comes the family list: Esau's sons, his grandsons, and the chiefs they become in the land of Edom. One standout: Timna, a concubine of Esau's son Eliphaz, gives birth to Amalek. That's a LOT of chiefs. My bakery has one chief, and he's the guy on the gold base talking to you.

Next, the Horites, the sons of Seir who were living in the land, along with their chiefs. Tucked in there is Anah, who found the hot springs in the wilderness while pasturing his father Zibeon's donkeys. Out minding donkeys, and he finds HOT SPRINGS. Best day at work anybody ever had.

Then a list of the kings who reigned in Edom before any king reigned over the Israelites. Eight kings in all, and after Bela, each new king takes over when the one before him dies. One of them, Hadad son of Bedad, defeated Midian in the country of Moab.
The chapter wraps up with one more list of Esau's chiefs by their families and regions, eleven names in all. And the last line sums up the whole thing: Esau was the father of the Edomites.
